claims.text: High-energy mechanical alloying followed by rapid spark plasma sintering can suppress porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed processing route will produce a fine-grained nanocrystalline solid solution dominated by FCC with minor BCC.
The proposed processing route will suppress formation of a brittle HCP phase associated with Ti-rich systems.
Dual-phase FCC-BCC stability is maximized at an SPS temperature of 900–1100 °C and a heating rate above 100 °C/min.
Keeping the sintering strain rate below 10^-3 s^-1 minimizes cracking caused by thermal-expansion mismatch.
Mechanical alloying for 40 h at 250 RPM provides sufficient severe plastic deformation to homogenize the alloy.
Homogenization and severe plastic deformation during mechanical alloying suppress HCP nucleation.
SPS at 900–1100 °C with a heating rate above 100 °C/min and a 5 min dwell achieves full density.
Rapid SPS retains grain refinement without significant phase decomposition.
The processed alloy will have hardness above 600 HV0.5.
The processed alloy will have porosity below 1%.
The predicted hardness increase results from a combination of grain refinement and solute strengthening.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has porosity and hardness of approximately 200 HV0.5.
Ti content must remain below 15 at.% to avoid HCP dominance.
A cooling rate above 10 °C/min prevents HCP formation.
Insufficiently optimized SPS parameters may leave residual porosity.
Insufficient cooling rates may permit HCP formation.
Nanoindentation at 10 mN with a 10 s dwell, combined with TEM verification of grain refinement, can test the proposed hardness mechanism.
Failure of hardness to increase with TEM-verified grain refinement would falsify the claim that hardness is due to solute strengthening rather than grain refinement.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes hardness to both grain refinement and solute strengthening, but the falsification statement instead refers to falsifying a claim that hardness is due to solute strengthening rather than grain refinement. This reverses the requested attribution and does not cleanly test the stated combined mechanism.

The predicted hardness is specified as HV0.5, whereas the proposed falsification uses 10 mN nanoindentation. These different load regimes are not directly interchangeable without a conversion or indentation-size-effect analysis.
